Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES ‐ July 1, 2021

A meeting of the Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission was convened on July 1, 2021 via
Zoom. Commissioner Denmon called the meeting to order at 6:13 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Roll Call

Present
  Commissioner Henry Brown, Commissioner at Large
  Commissioner Lee Denmon, District One
  Commissioner Cynthia McLemore, District Three
  Sabrina Barnes, Director - Parks, Recreation and Community Services
  Teresa Estrada, Recreation Superintendent
  Juan Mata, Parks Supervisor
  Thomas Uwal, Human Services Superintendent
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
Absent
  Commissioner Jacob Fragoso, District Two
  Commissioner Christopher Beck, District Four

Public Comments

  None

Approval of the Minutes

  Commissioner Brown made a motion to approve the minutes from June 3, 2021.
Commissioner McLemore seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Brown, McLemore and Denmon
  Nays: None

Staff Report

  Stephanie Maldonado introduced a staff report recommending the Park and Recreation
Commission recommend the Mayor and Council Members take the following actions: 1. Adopt a
resolution amending the Fiscal Year 2020-2021 budget to cover expenditures for prevailing wage
adjustments and change orders the Park Restroom Improvement Project Phase I - Rogers Park
(General Fund Reserves); and 2. Approve payment of an invoice for prevailing wage adjustments
and change orders in the amount of $77,103.96 to ABC Builders, Incorporation for the Rogers Park
Restroom Project, CB-19-14. (General Fund Reserves)

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES ‐ July 1, 2021

  Commissioner Brown made a motion to approve the staff report and Commissioner
McLemore seconded. The motion was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Brown, McLemore and Denmon
  Nays: None

Verbal Reports

  Juan Mata gave a verbal report on behalf of the Parks Administration regarding the following:
    The Parks Division staff has revitalized the playground surfacing at Queen and North Parks
  by adding 20 yards of wood fiber. They also added 10 yards of decomposed granite on the
  walking trail at North Park.
    During the month of June, the City experienced heavy graffiti in District 4 near Yukon Avenue
  and Crenshaw Boulevard. Edward Vincent Park has also been heavily tagged inside the
  restrooms. Staff has begun repainting the restrooms.

  Commissioner Denmon asked about staff’s involvement with the Little Library located at
North Park. He stated that the glass door appears to be broken. Director Barnes acknowledged
Commissioner Demon’s statement and gave a brief overview of an upcoming beautification project
happening at North Park. The project will be done by volunteers from the SoFi Stadium and part of
the project includes improving the Little Library, some planting and other sprucing up of the park.
Staff will visit the park on July 2, 2021 to repair the window and ensure there aren’t any safety risks.
If no risks are identified, all clean-up will take place on July 16, 2021.

  Stephanie Maldonado gave a verbal report on behalf of the Recreation Division regarding
the following:
   Drive-In Movies in the Park: Join the Parks, Recreation and Community Services
  Department for Drive-In Movies at the Park. All movies will be shown on the big screen at
  Edward Vincent Park in the Champions Field Parking Lot. Gates open at 6:30 p.m. and all
  movies begin at dusk. The cost is $15 per vehicle and tickets must be purchased online in
  advance at parksrec.cityofinglewood.org. This year’s movies will feature Trolls World Tour
  on July 17 and Sonic the Hedgehog on Saturday, July 31. All movies are rated PG. Food
  trucks will be on site and refreshments will be available for purchase. Bring 10 recyclable
  items and receive a free gift. If your schedule permits, consider joining us for an
  unforgettable evening of cinema in your car!
   Re-Opening of Recreation Centers: Parks and Recreation Centers are currently open daily
  from 9:00 a.m. – 6:00 p.m. for summer day camp participants only. We will re-open to the
  general public from 6:00 p.m. – 8:00 p.m. beginning Monday, July 19. Due to the current
  summer camp protocols, we are limited to the number of persons allowed in the building.
  After the culmination of camp, we will resume normal business hours – Monday thru Friday
  from 8:00 a.m. – 8:00 p.m. and Saturday from 8:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. The full re-opening will
  begin on Monday, August 16th.

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES ‐ July 1, 2021

    Swimming Pool Hours on 4th of July: The Edward Vincent Park Swim Complex will be open
  on the 4th of July. There will be two swim sessions available: 11:30 a.m. – 1:30 p.m. and
  2:00 p.m. – 4:00 p.m. Reservations are required. Reservations can be made at
  parksrec.cityofinglewood.org.

  Commissioner Denmon requested for staff to take a look at the swimming pool, stating the
deeper end of the pool’s pumps don’t seem to be functioning properly but the shallow end of the pool
looks great. Sabrina Barnes stated an acid wash is needed on that end of the pool. There was a
malfunctioning of the pool’s pumps resulting in a staining. Staff tried a gentle treatment but it was
unsuccessful. Treatment continues. The remaining option will be to drain the pool completely in
order to perform the acid wash which will take four to five days. We do not have that window of time
to do that now but as soon as we get downtime, it will be done.

  Thomas Uwal gave a verbal report on behalf of the Human Services Division regarding the
following:
   The Summer Food Summer Program (SFSP) is operating at City Parks and Community
  Centers five (5) days a week, Monday through Friday, from June 14, 2021, through August
  20, 2021. We are providing breakfast from 9:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m., and lunch and snacks
  from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. at the following sites:
  a. Ashwood Park
  b. Crenshaw-Imperial Library
  c. Darby Park
  d. Edward Vincent, Jr. Park
  e. Lockhaven Community Center
  f. Rogers Park
  g. Siminski Park
   The Transportation Program continues to provide transportation for doctor’s appointments
  and critical appointments such as dialysis. A recent visual inspection of all I-Line shuttle bus
  stop signs was conducted to ensure all signs were in place and visual to the public.
   A Metro Comprehensive Survey for Transportation and the Senior Center facility relating to
  ADA regulations was completed and submitted to Metro who is our funding source. We are
  looking forward to the being approved by Metro in the near future.
   Senior Center Programs/Activities: We are planning to open limited activities and programs
  at the Senior Center on July 19, 2021. We do not have a set date for a complete opening
  but we are developing a safe re-opening plan for the center. The few activities we are
  planning to open in Phase One (1) are Yoga, Zumba, Tai Chi and exercise classes. With the
  remaining activities to open in the third phase as we are adhering to Los Angeles County
  Guidelines. We are also planning to open computer classes, the gym and the billiard room
  all while being responsible.
  This portion of the report was inaudible.
   The Senior Center was recently equipped with self-monitoring temperature stations and staff
  has since been utilizing this new tool. All staff has returned to duty onsite as of June 15,

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES ‐ July 1, 2021

  2021. As we move closer to a soft opening, we want to ensure it is safe to do so for our
  seniors.
    Currently the Nutrition Program has 490 seniors enrolled in the Elderly Nutrition Program
  (ENP). A total of 3,430 meals per week are distributed to our seniors. The dining room will
  remain closed until further notice is given by Los Angeles County. Once we are granted
  approval we will begin with a grab and go service.
    The Nutrition program collaborated with one of our senior meal providers who worked with
  LA County to produce videos encouraging our seniors and the community to get vaccinated
  for COVID. Representatives from staff, seniors and community participated in the 60-second
  video. All did a great job communicating the message to the community. You can view the
  video at the following link https://vimeo.com/563493811/cc31a74586

  Commissioner McLemore asked for clarification of the Senior Center’s reopening. Thomas
Uwal stated we anticipate opening date on July 19, 2021, offering seniors limited classes on a first
come first serve basis. The classes will include Yoga, Zumba, Tai Chi and an exercise class. The
computer room, gym and billboards room will also be open. Seniors must call and make an
appointment prior to their visit. Director Barnes added lounging/gathering at the center will not be
permitted. All guests must be attending class or visiting with a purpose. The center will not be a social
setting at this time.

Director’s Business

  Sabrina Barnes stated our Department is working with the Public Works Department to
submit an application to the County for the Edward Vincent, Jr. Park Storm Water Improvement
Project. The project will provide significant benefits to local communities and in an underserved area
of the Inglewood as it relates to the large Ballona Creek water shell. The proposed project will
capture, treat, and infiltrate storm water at Edward Vincent, Jr. Park to reduce metals, bacteria,
toxins, and other pollutants that are draining into Centinela Creek. To achieve these objectives, the
City of Inglewood plans to construct an underground infiltration gallery below the baseball diamonds
at the park, add a dry creek that will run through the center of the park, and a bio retention area to
manage storm water using nature-based solutions. Development of the dry creek through the park
will reintroduce the historical creek feature that previously existed at the site. In addition to providing
substantial water quality improvements, the project provides valuable amenities for the local
community, including overall enhanced aesthetics, walking trails, new sports fields, lighting and
safety enhancements, and additional shade trees. This project will take a lot of planning and money
so as we start the application process the timeline, if successful, is expected to be realized in four
(4) to five (5) years.

  In the meantime, our department continues to work on Measure A funding which Sabrina
Barnes spoke about at the last meeting. Measure A requires community input meetings. Ms. Barnes
reminded the Commission of the priority list that was established in 2015 and last updated in 2019.
A 2021 priority list is needed to apply for Measure A funding. We have approximately $1.5 million

  4
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES ‐ July 1, 2021

dollars sitting in the bank and in order to acquire funds we are required to get community input as
well as complete and submit applications. She hopes the restrooms remain a priority as well as the
ball fields and other areas previously listed that are in need of improvement. Measure A passed by
voters in 2016, is similar to Proposition A which ended in 2019. It allows us to have per capita funds,
meaning every year we’ll receive a pool of funding along with competitive grants. The August
Commission meeting will be more hands-on consisting of a presentation to inform the community
about Measure A, project completions, previously prioritized projects and allow voters to add any
other projects to the list as they see fit. Voting will be conducted by a quick survey most likely via
chat where individuals would be able to click the link provided choosing their top three choices,
projects will be ranked by percentages. Still researching the logistics of how to gather the information
virtually whether by polls or survey links either way feedback from the community is needed. Within
the next two (2) to three (3) weeks, information will be provided to the Commission to provide to the
attendees of your choice. We will need an audience/community participation to make suggestions
and respond to what our priorities are. Director Barnes knows that Commissioner Denmon has been
surveying the parks and asked the other Commissioners to be prepared to share what they think is
priority in their District or globally.

  Commissioner Denmon asked for clarification of the location of the new restroom budgeted
to be built. Director Barnes stated the new restrooms will be built at Edward Vincent Park. The Public
Works Department has developed the plans and specifications. A few minor revisions were
requested by the City Manager to ensure maximum space to allow for additional restrooms and which
is also more economical. The expectation of encumbrance is 30 to 60 days with the refining of the
bid specifications, with hopes of the Commission making that recommendation at our next meeting.
Community Development Block Program (CDBG) will be awarding us just under $600,000.00 for the
next fiscal year. Director Barnes hope is to fund another restroom at Edward Vincent Park and
restrooms at Darby Park simultaneously with the funding from Measure A. The remaining restrooms
that would be in need of improvement would be five (5) at Edward Vincent, two (2) at Darby leaving
Queen Park to be last on the list for a total renovation of the entire park site. Commissioner
McLemore asked Director Barnes for clarification on the design and layout of the restroom at Edward
Vincent Park. Director Barnes stated the layout will be different from Rogers Park. Edward Vincent
Park has more restrooms and the goal is to be more efficient with spacing and funding.
Commissioner Brown thanked staff for the indepth report and shared his concerns about the senior
transportation being affected by traffic down Century Boulevard near the SoFi Stadium. He is pleased
to see Director Barnes providing quality programs, utilizing grants and gives his full support to staff.
Director Barnes stated efforts are being coordinated to minimize any impact on residents and
Thomas Uwal and his team are always looking for ways to ensure transportation isn’t impacted by
any activities. The Parking and Traffic Enforcement has been doing a great job with keeping staff
informed of current and upcoming events enabling us to plan accordingly. Commissioner Denmon
stated that Council is working to make the city 5G which will assist in identifying areas with heavier
traffic during different times and will also assist the traffic lights aiding the traffic flow. Commissioner
Denmon assured Commissioner Brown there will be a follow up on his concerns when the time
comes.

  5
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES ‐ July 1, 2021

Public Comments

  None

Commissioners Comments

  Commissioner Brown commended staff who through the pandemic, continued to function
and provide quality services to the community.

  Commissioner Denmon agreed with Commissioner Brown stating Director Barnes, her staff,
the graffiti team, transportation and everyone is doing a great job ensuring our parks are functional,
clean. The upcoming projects are only going to make them better.

  Commissioner Denmon asked about the Willie Agee funds for the Playhouse. Director
Barnes stated those funds will go into our nonprofit, the Inglewood Community Services Corporation.
A request has been made to apply the funds towards an HVAC System, windows and or lighting. A
recent amendment was made to the budget made monies available for the HVAC system so we
hope that Mr. Agee’s funds can be used for special programs which she will discuss with the
Playhouse Manager, Shelli Boone.

  Commissioner Denmon wished everyone a happy and safe 4th of July and asked that
everyone be vigilant and pay attention to what’s going on in their community.

With no further comments the meeting was adjourned at 6:49 p.m.
